problem: When the request is untagged, task-new tells the model to omit `--tag`. `cmd_branch` then reads stdin, and the documented invocation has no stdin redirect. The open-pipe hang that PR #192 fixed only for the `--tag` path comes back here.
failure: Give a request with no clear [type]. The model follows line 77, drops `--tag`, and runs `python3 "$NODES" branch --title "..."` with an inherited open stdin pipe. `_read_stdin_lines()` calls `sys.stdin.read()`, which blocks forever, so Step 0 hangs.
fix: Add `< /dev/null` to the documented invocation, or always pass `--tag fix` explicitly.

problem: The heading cascade climbs past the h2 group to the document's `# Backlog` title and deletes that too. prune-backlog then writes a zero-byte backlog.md, which breaks the SKILL contract that backlog.md 'never' goes away.
failure:
`prune_lines("# Backlog

## G

- [ ] x
", ["- [ ] x"])` returns `''`. `_write_or_delete(..., delete_if_empty=False)` then truncates backlog.md to 0 bytes and the `# Backlog` title is lost.
fix: Stop the cascade at h1, or never remove the document title.

problem: After dropping a heading, the cascade takes the nearest preceding live heading as the next candidate, whatever its level. That can be a same-level sibling instead of the parent. A sibling that was already empty before the run gets deleted, which breaks the invariant that a heading empty before the run is left alone.
failure: Input: `## Placeholder` (empty) / `## Live` / `- [ ] x` / `## Other` / `- [ ] y`. Pruning `- [ ] x` also deletes `## Placeholder`.
fix: For the parent lookup, pick the nearest preceding heading whose level is lower than the dropped heading's level.

problem: `prune_h1_block` deletes everything up to the next h1. A `## Review Backlog` appended after the Sprint Contract h1 is wiped along with it, and its open findings are lost. This differs from reconcile-harness.py's `strip_sprint_block`, which documents this hazard.
failure: tasks.md contains `# Sprint: x` / `status: done` / `## Review Backlog` / `### PR #99` / `- [ ] f`. `prune-tasks --block "Sprint: x"` returns `''` and deletes tasks.md with the open finding inside.
fix: End the block at the next heading of any level that is not part of the sprint, or reuse the `strip_sprint_block` logic.

problem: `slugify` keeps only ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9]`, so a non-ASCII title gives an empty slug and `branch` exits 1. task-next and task-new SKILL.md also lack the empty-BRANCH guard.
failure: `branch_name("로그인 오류 수정", [], tag="FIX")` returns `('', 'Title produced an empty slug')`. `git checkout -b ""` then fails. A mixed title such as `로그인 fix` silently becomes `fix/fix`.
fix: Fall back to a deterministic slug, such as a hash or date, for non-ASCII titles, and add the `[[ -n "$BRANCH" ]]` guard.

problem: The `--tag` value is lowercased but never stripped of brackets or validated. Following the instruction 'Pass the `[type]` inferred in Step 1' literally produces an invalid git ref.
fix: Strip the brackets and validate the tag against the allowed set.

problem: `prune_lines` deletes only the `- [ ]` line itself. The item's indented continuation lines stay behind, attach to the previous item or heading, and keep an emptied heading alive.
failure: Input: `## G` / `- [ ] [FIX] a` / `  - acceptance: foo` / `- [ ] [FIX] b`. Pruning `a` leaves `  - acceptance: foo` orphaned under `## G`.
fix: Also remove the indented continuation lines that follow the pruned item.

problem: `_region_blank` treats a `---` horizontal-rule separator as content. Emptied headings therefore survive, and tasks.md is never deleted once only separators remain.
failure: Input: `## Review Backlog` / `### PR #99` / `- [ ] one` / `---` / `# Sprint: x`. Pruning `- [ ] one` leaves an empty `### PR #99`. `prune_h1_block` leaves `---\n\n`, so tasks.md is never deleted.
fix: Treat `---` separators as blank in `_region_blank` and in the emptiness check.

problem: A partially tagged group uses the shared tag. The docstring and the replaced prose rule both say mixed or absent tags fall back to `fix`.
failure: `[FEAT]` plus an untagged item gives `feat/...`, but the documented rule requires `fix/`.
fix: Use the common tag only when every item carries it; otherwise fall back to `fix`.

problem: When `## Unreleased` exists but is empty, the entry is inserted directly above the next heading with no blank line between them.
failure:
`# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 4.0.0
` becomes `...- [done] x (2026)
## 4.0.0
`, with the heading glued to the list item.
fix: Insert a blank line between the new entry and the following heading.
